note: Baked by tools/atmos/bake.py (reduced moist-air solver; see MODEL-NOTES-ATMOS.md)

steam_pipe.title: Pipe / vent steam jet
steam_pipe.size_note: vertical jet from a 0.2 m vent, plume 1.5 to 2 m tall, clear gap about 10 to 20 cm

main.encoding: WebP lossy RGBA; rgb = grey, sRGB-encoded (use an sRGB texture); alpha = straight (non-premultiplied) coverage
main.blend: normal: (SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); or premultiply on load and use (ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)

scatter.encoding: grey WebP, same frame order as main at 0.5x size (low: 0.25x); value = forward-scatter strength 0..1
scatter.blend: additive on top of main: out += sunColour * scatter * sunBacklight * gain; mask with the main alpha so it never extends past the sprite

heat.encoding: grey WebP at 0.25x; heat = (value/255)^(1/0.8); 1.0 = th_ref kelvin above ambient

steam_pipe.anchor_note: anchor = [u, v] of the emitter / ground contact inside a frame, from the top-left corner

wind.note: plume bends over: lean the quad about its anchor
wind.note_base: plume bends over: lean the quad about its anchor

night.note: steam is lit by fires and lamps only: add the local light colour

thermal.note: steam is bright in thermal view: draw the heat layer through a white-hot palette, scaled by the alpha; the visible fog is irrelevant to the sensor

night_vision.note: steam is a soft grey cloud; add the scatter layer at 0.5 where IR illuminators hit it

haze.note: attach a DIST.haze source above the vent: strength, radius_m and height_m (the invisible hot gas is hotter than the visible plume), drifting up at rise_speed_mps; fade with the stage (start ramps in, fade ramps out)

mirror_variants.note: every loop clip may also be drawn mirrored (scale.x = -1) for twice as many looks; variants above are distinct simulation windows
